And it will happen. Maybe not in my lifetime, but it's a certainty. Humans are explorers, even if politicians don't always want to fund exploration.

Similar 3D printing techniques are being developed for lunar materials: http://sservi.nasa.gov/articles/building-a-lunar-base-with-3d-printing/

Also, although you're right that attempting to colonize Mars first would be a big mistake, the problem is not just getting out of Earth's gravity well. Getting from Earth orbit into Mars orbit does require more delta-v than getting into lunar orbit, but not vastly more: http://www.projectrho.com/public_html/rocket/images/mission/solarSubway.jpg. Mars' gravity well is much harder to get into (and out of) that the moon's. Then there's the trip time (~six months in each direction).

I believe that with an established base they'll be able to provide more of the high mass items (water from ice mining) and also create useful materials for the next step up to Mars.
